title: MHA Designates 23 Pakistan-Based Individuals as Terrorists Under UAPA
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has designated 23 Pakistan-based individuals as terrorists under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The list includes operatives of Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba, among them Hafiz Saeed's son-in-law and an individual linked to reconnoitring the Ram Temple. The designations cite connections to attacks in Jammu & Kashmir. This is part of India's post-Pahalgam attack crackdown on cross-border terror networks.
exam_angle: Tests knowledge of UAPA provisions (Sections 35-36 on terrorist designation), the role of MHA in internal security, and India's counter-terrorism legal framework. Also relevant to India-Pakistan relations and J&K security.
key_facts: 23 individuals designated terrorists under UAPA by MHA
Includes Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba operatives
Hafiz Saeed's son-in-law included in the list
UAPA Sections 35-36 govern individual terrorist designation in India

title: Monsoon Session of Parliament 2026 to Begin July 20, Conclude August 13
summary: The Monsoon Session of the Indian Parliament has been scheduled to commence on July 20, 2026, and will run until August 13, 2026. This is one of the three regular sessions of Parliament held annually. The session is expected to see significant legislative business including pending Bills and budgetary discussions. The dates were confirmed by government sources.
exam_angle: Parliamentary sessions are a standard polity topic; aspirants must know the three sessions (Budget, Monsoon, Winter) and the constitutional provisions for summoning Parliament (Article 85). The Monsoon Session often passes key legislation.
key_facts: Monsoon Session 2026: July 20 to August 13
Parliament summoned under Article 85 by President on advice of Cabinet
Three regular sessions: Budget (Feb–May), Monsoon (Jul–Aug), Winter (Nov–Dec)
Gap between two sessions cannot exceed six months (constitutional requirement)

title: India's Indus Waters Treaty Stand Unchanged Amid Pakistan Threats
summary: India has reaffirmed that its position on the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) remains unchanged despite threats from Pakistan following heightened bilateral tensions post-Pahalgam attack. India had earlier served notice to renegotiate or suspend the treaty. An Indian envoy also stated there is no need for India to emulate Pakistan's role in Iran mediation. The stand reflects India's hardened diplomatic posture towards Pakistan.
exam_angle: The Indus Waters Treaty (1960, World Bank-brokered) is a perennial GS Paper 2 topic on India-Pakistan relations and river-water disputes. The current suspension/renegotiation controversy is highly exam-relevant.
key_facts: Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960, brokered by World Bank
India served notice to renegotiate IWT after Pahalgam attack 2025
India's current stand: position on IWT 'unchanged'
Treaty allocates eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India; western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan

title: Iran: Ayatollah Khamenei's State Funeral Held in Tehran
summary: Iran held a weeklong state funeral for Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran, with millions of mourners gathering for the procession. Khamenei, who led Iran since 1989, died following a US-Israel military strike on Iran's nuclear and military infrastructure. The funeral comes at a critical juncture for the West Asian region, with Iran's political succession now a major geopolitical concern. US President Trump also commented on the strikes that led to his death.
exam_angle: Iran's Supreme Leader position (Velayat-e-Faqih system), Iran's nuclear programme, and West Asia geopolitics are important IR topics. India's energy security via Strait of Hormuz is a GS Paper 3 linkage.
key_facts: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was Iran's Supreme Leader since 1989
Iran's political system: Supreme Leader (Velayat-e-Faqih) is highest authority above President
India imports significant crude oil from the Gulf region via Strait of Hormuz
Khamenei's death has created a major geopolitical power vacuum in West Asia

title: India's Forex Reserves Fall $5.65 Billion Amid Iran War Fallout
summary: India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $5.65 billion, attributed to the impact of the Iran-Israel conflict on global oil prices and financial markets. Rising crude oil import costs are straining India's current account. The rupee also weakened against the dollar in the same period. India navigated the Strait of Hormuz energy crisis with measures described by PM Modi as keeping citizen burden minimal.
exam_angle: Forex reserves management, current account deficit, and energy import vulnerability are core GS Paper 3 economy topics. The Hormuz crisis linkage also connects to India's energy security policy.
key_facts: Forex reserves fell by $5.65 billion due to Iran war impact
India's forex reserves managed by RBI
Strait of Hormuz: ~20% of global oil trade passes through it
Rupee weakened amid global uncertainty; Sensex rallied for 4th consecutive week

title: India Sets $1 Trillion Export Target for FY2026 as Trade Rises
summary: India has set an ambitious $1 trillion export target for FY2025-26 as both merchandise and services trade showed an upward trend. The government is counting on strong services exports (particularly IT and business services) and a recovering global demand for goods to meet this goal. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal also indicated that an India-Peru Free Trade Agreement is not imminent. The target aligns with India's broader goal of becoming a major global trading nation.
exam_angle: India's export targets, trade policy, and FTA strategy are important for GS Paper 3. The $1 trillion target and the composition of India's export basket (merchandise vs services) are likely MCQ/mains data points.
key_facts: India's export target for FY26: $1 trillion (merchandise + services combined)
India's services exports driven by IT, BPO, and professional services
India-Peru FTA: Commerce Minister says not happening anytime soon
Ministry of Commerce and Industry oversees India's export promotion

title: India-France Economic and Financial Dialogue Co-Chaired by Nirmala Sitharaman in Aix-en-Provence
summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman co-chaired the India-France Economic and Financial Dialogue (EFD) with French Minister Roland Lescure in Aix-en-Provence, France. The dialogue covered bilateral economic cooperation, investment flows, digital finance, and industrial partnership. France is one of India's key strategic partners in Europe and a member of the G7. The EFD is a high-level bilateral mechanism for economic coordination.
exam_angle: India-France bilateral relations, strategic partnership mechanisms, and financial diplomacy are relevant to GS Paper 2 (IR). France is also a key partner in India's defence procurement and nuclear energy cooperation.
key_facts: India-France EFD co-chaired by Nirmala Sitharaman and Roland Lescure
Venue: Aix-en-Provence, France
India and France have a Strategic Partnership since 1998
France is a key partner in defence (Rafale jets, submarines) and nuclear energy

title: Centre Clears Four China-Linked Firms for Critical Power Sector Tenders
summary: The Central government has allowed four Chinese-linked firms to participate in critical power sector tenders, reversing earlier restrictions that blocked Chinese companies from strategic infrastructure projects. The move has drawn political opposition from Congress, which termed it a security risk. India had tightened FDI rules from China in 2020 under Press Note 3, requiring government approval for investments from border-sharing nations. India's envoy to China simultaneously noted that more Chinese investment is beneficial for the broader relationship.
exam_angle: India's FDI policy vis-à-vis China (Press Note 3, 2020), energy sector security, and India-China economic relations are high-priority GS Paper 3/IR topics. The tension between economic pragmatism and national security is a key mains theme.
key_facts: Centre allowed 4 Chinese-linked firms into power sector tenders
Press Note 3 (2020): mandates government approval for FDI from countries sharing land borders with India
India-China FDI normalisation linked to post-Galwan disengagement process
India's envoy to China stated more Chinese investment is good for bilateral ties

title: India Investigates Tata Data Leak Exposing Apple iPhone Manufacturing Secrets
summary: Indian authorities are investigating a significant data breach at Tata Electronics, which manufactures Apple iPhones in India, that exposed sensitive production and supply chain secrets. The leak raised concerns about the security of India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem, which is being positioned as an alternative to China under the PLI scheme. The incident has implications for Apple's vendor confidentiality and India's credibility as a global electronics hub. Tata Electronics is one of the first Indian companies to manufacture iPhones.
exam_angle: India's electronics PLI scheme, Make in India, data security, and the role of Tata/Apple partnership in boosting domestic manufacturing are relevant to GS Paper 3. Data protection laws (DPDP Act 2023) are also a linkage.
key_facts: Data breach at Tata Electronics exposed Apple iPhone manufacturing secrets
Tata Electronics: first Indian company to manufacture iPhones (from 2023)
India's PLI scheme for mobile manufacturing aims to attract global supply chains
Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP) 2023 governs data security in India

title: Government Considers Separate Legal Framework for Artificial Intelligence
summary: The Indian government is evaluating the creation of a separate legal framework for Artificial Intelligence (AI), with the IT Secretary indicating that evolving AI technology and risks such as deepfakes, cyber threats, and algorithmic bias may necessitate dedicated legislation. Currently, AI is regulated under existing IT laws and sector-specific guidelines. The Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY) has already issued non-binding AI advisory guidelines. India has so far preferred a 'light-touch' regulatory approach to AI.
exam_angle: AI regulation, digital governance, and India's technology policy are increasingly important for GS Paper 3. The contrast between India's non-binding advisory approach and the EU AI Act's binding framework is a relevant comparative angle.
key_facts: Government considering a separate AI law; currently regulated under IT Act 2000
MeitY issued AI advisory (April 2024) requiring government approval for AI tools in testing phase
Key AI risks cited: deepfakes, cyber threats, algorithmic bias
EU AI Act (2024) is the world's first comprehensive binding AI law — contrast with India's approach

title: MIB Sends 15-Day Notice to Telegram to Curb Pirated Content
summary: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB) has issued a notice to the messaging platform Telegram, setting a 15-day deadline to take proactive measures against pirated content circulating on its platform. MIB has sought an action report from Telegram on steps taken to prevent copyright infringement. This is part of India's intensified crackdown on digital piracy, which affects the film, music, and publishing industries. The action falls under the Copyright Act and IT Act provisions.
exam_angle: Digital regulation, intermediary liability, and copyright enforcement are important for GS Paper 3 (Sci-Tech/Economy). The role of MIB and India's evolving digital content governance framework are relevant policy dimensions.
key_facts: Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB) issued notice to Telegram
15-day deadline to curb pirated content and submit action report
Telegram has over 900 million global users; widely used for content sharing in India
IT Act 2000 (intermediary liability) and Copyright Act 1957 are the relevant legal frameworks

title: India Removes Chinese Battery-Linked Apps After E-Rickshaw Hack Incident
summary: The Indian government ordered the removal of Chinese-origin battery management apps after a Bluetooth-based hack allowed pranksters to remotely disable e-rickshaws in Delhi, stalling traffic and reducing driver earnings. Affected e-rickshaw drivers saw daily earnings drop from ₹1,000 to ₹600. The apps were linked to lithium battery management systems sourced from China. The incident has renewed scrutiny of Chinese software embedded in Indian mobility infrastructure.
exam_angle: Cybersecurity vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure, India's dependency on Chinese hardware/software in EVs, and data security policy are GS Paper 3 themes. The incident also highlights EV ecosystem regulation gaps.
key_facts: Chinese battery management apps removed after Bluetooth hack disabled Delhi e-rickshaws
Hack reduced e-rickshaw driver earnings from ₹1,000 to ₹600/day
Apps linked to lithium battery systems sourced from China
Raises questions about cybersecurity in India's EV/mobility infrastructure

title: PM Modi Launches India's First Greenfield Refinery-Petrochemical Complex in Rajasthan
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated India's first Greenfield integrated refinery and petrochemical hub in Rajasthan, marking a significant milestone in India's energy and chemical manufacturing ambitions. The complex is expected to reduce India's dependence on imported petrochemicals and strengthen the domestic chemicals industry. PM Modi also stated that India navigated the Strait of Hormuz energy crisis with minimal burden on citizens, citing strategic petroleum reserves and fuel pricing measures.
exam_angle: India's energy security, refinery capacity, petrochemical industry under Make in India, and strategic petroleum reserves are GS Paper 3 topics. Greenfield vs brownfield investment concepts are also relevant.
key_facts: India's first Greenfield refinery-petrochemical complex inaugurated in Rajasthan by PM Modi
Aims to reduce India's reliance on imported petrochemicals
India maintains Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR) at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, and Padur
India is the world's third-largest oil consumer and importer

title: A New Chapter in India's Nuclear Journey: PIB
summary: The Press Information Bureau (PIB) published a feature titled 'A New Chapter in India's Nuclear Journey,' highlighting recent developments in India's civilian nuclear energy programme. India is expanding its nuclear capacity as part of its low-carbon energy transition, with plans to increase nuclear power share in the electricity mix. The Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) oversees India's nuclear programme, which includes NPCIL-run reactors and indigenous development of Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs).
exam_angle: India's nuclear energy policy, the three-stage nuclear programme, NPCIL, and nuclear as part of India's clean energy transition are important GS Paper 3 (Energy/Sci-Tech) topics. India's nuclear doctrine and safeguards are also relevant.
key_facts: India's nuclear programme governed by Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)
Three-stage nuclear programme: PHWRs → Fast Breeder Reactors → Thorium-based reactors
NPCIL operates civilian nuclear power plants
India has ~7,480 MW installed nuclear capacity (about 3% of electricity mix); target to expand significantly

title: Sri Lanka Upgraded to Upper-Middle Income; India's Classification Unchanged Despite Growth
summary: The World Bank has reclassified Sri Lanka as an upper-middle-income country, a significant economic milestone following the island nation's recovery from its 2022 debt crisis. India, despite strong GDP growth of 7-8% as noted by US President Trump, remains classified as a lower-middle-income country. The World Bank uses Gross National Income (GNI) per capita thresholds for income classification, reviewed annually. India's large population keeps its per capita income below the upper-middle threshold.
exam_angle: World Bank income classifications, GNI per capita thresholds, and India's position in global economic rankings are standard GS Paper 3 data points. The contrast between GDP growth rate and per capita income is an important conceptual distinction.
key_facts: World Bank income groups: Low (<$1,145 GNI/capita), Lower-Middle ($1,146–$4,515), Upper-Middle ($4,516–$14,005), High (>$14,005)
Sri Lanka reclassified as Upper-Middle Income country
India remains Lower-Middle Income despite ~7-8% GDP growth
Trump acknowledged India growing at 7-8%, walked back earlier 'dead economy' remark

title: Tech Layoffs in First Half of 2026 Exceed All of 2025; India Second-Worst Hit
summary: Global technology sector layoffs in the first half of 2026 have already surpassed the total layoffs recorded throughout all of 2025, according to a new report. India is the second-worst affected country globally after the United States, with thousands of IT sector employees losing jobs amid automation, AI-driven workforce restructuring, and cost-cutting by major tech firms. Simultaneously, AI-focused hiring is outpacing overall IT recruitment in India, creating a skills mismatch.
exam_angle: Structural unemployment, technology-driven job displacement, India's IT sector dependence, and the AI-employment paradox are relevant GS Paper 3 (Economy/Sci-Tech) themes important for essay and mains answers.
key_facts: H1 2026 tech layoffs globally exceed entire 2025 total
India is second-worst affected country after the US in tech layoffs
AI hiring in India outpacing overall IT sector recruitment (separate report)
43% of Indian firms use AI but workforce readiness still lags (India Today report)

title: First Season's Low-Pressure Area Forms Over Bay of Bengal; Red Alerts Issued for Odisha and Mumbai
summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) reported the formation of the season's first low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal, triggering heavy rainfall warnings. Red alerts were issued for five districts in Odisha, and Mumbai was placed on red alert for extremely heavy rainfall. IMD also issued rain warnings for Konkan and the Western Ghats. Low-pressure areas over the Bay of Bengal are a primary mechanism driving monsoon rainfall over the Indian subcontinent.
exam_angle: Monsoon meteorology, the role of the Bay of Bengal in driving Indian monsoon, IMD warning systems (colour-coded alerts), and disaster preparedness are important GS Paper 1/3 topics. Low-pressure areas and cyclogenesis are standard geography concepts.
key_facts: Season's first low-pressure area formed over Bay of Bengal (July 2026)
IMD red alert issued for 5 Odisha districts and Mumbai
IMD colour-coded alerts: Green (no warning), Yellow (watch), Orange (alert), Red (warning — take action)
Bay of Bengal supplies moisture for ~80% of India's monsoon rainfall

title: Europe Heatwave 2026: France Reports 30% Rise in Deaths as Temperatures Shatter Records
summary: Europe is experiencing a severe heatwave in 2026, with France reporting a 30% rise in heat-related deaths compared to previous years as temperatures break historical records. The heatwave is being attributed to climate change-driven shifts in weather patterns, including a weakened jet stream. The event underscores the accelerating frequency and intensity of extreme heat events globally, consistent with IPCC projections. European nations have activated emergency heat action plans.
exam_angle: Climate change impacts, extreme weather events, urban heat islands, and global warming projections from IPCC are critical GS Paper 3 (Environment) topics. Heat mortality is an important dimension of climate adaptation discourse.
key_facts: Europe heatwave 2026: France reports 30% rise in heat-related deaths
Linked to climate change-driven jet stream weakening and blocking high-pressure systems
IPCC AR6 (2021-22): 1.5°C warming threshold increases extreme heat frequency significantly
Europe's 2003 heatwave killed ~70,000 people — a benchmark for climate mortality studies

title: Notorious Gangster Goldy Dhillon Arrested in Spain
summary: Goldy Dhillon, a notorious India-origin gangster believed to be operating from abroad and linked to multiple organized crime networks in India, was arrested in Spain. Dhillon is associated with criminal activities including extortion, contract killings, and links to cross-border crime syndicates. The arrest is significant in the context of India's efforts to extradite fugitive criminals from abroad and its growing law enforcement cooperation with European nations. Red Corner Notices through Interpol are typically used in such cases.
exam_angle: Extradition treaties, Interpol Red Corner Notices, organized crime and national security, and India's bilateral law enforcement cooperation are GS Paper 3/IR topics. Fugitive criminals abroad is a recurring mains theme.
key_facts: Goldy Dhillon arrested in Spain; linked to organized crime in India
India uses Interpol Red Corner Notices to seek arrest of fugitives abroad
India-Spain do not have a formal extradition treaty; mutual legal assistance possible
India has extradition treaties with ~50 countries; extradition from non-treaty countries possible via diplomatic channels

title: Bengaluru, Chandigarh, Delhi Top India's Average Income Rankings: Report
summary: A new report has ranked Bengaluru, Chandigarh, and Delhi as the top cities in India by average per capita income, reflecting the concentration of high-paying IT, government, and services sector jobs in these urban centres. The report highlights the growing urban-rural and inter-city income disparity in India. Bengaluru's position at the top is driven by its status as India's technology capital and startup ecosystem hub. The findings have implications for understanding India's uneven growth pattern.
exam_angle: Regional economic disparities, urbanisation, income inequality, and the role of cities in India's economic growth are GS Paper 1/3 themes. Such reports may appear as data sources in mains questions on economic geography.
key_facts: Top cities by average income: Bengaluru, Chandigarh, Delhi (Report, 2026)
Bengaluru is India's IT capital and leading startup hub
India's Gini coefficient indicates moderate-to-high income inequality
India's urban population: ~36% (Census 2011 data); projected to reach 50% by 2050
